subject: Taxes
title: Types of Income
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Types of Income.

hook.text: Not all income is taxed the same. Wages, investment gains, and rental income all face different rates and rules.

buildup.text: Ordinary income—wages, salaries, tips—is taxed at the standard progressive rates. This is how most people earn money.

discovery.text: Capital gains—profits from selling investments—get a lower rate: 0%, 15%, or 20%.

twist.text: Warren Buffett famously noted he pays a lower tax rate than his secretary.

climax.text: The different treatment of income types is why two people earning the same amount can pay wildly different taxes.

punchline.text: Same money, different source, different tax. Income type matters.

quiz.question: Why can investors pay a lower tax rate than workers?
options: Capital gains are taxed at lower rates than wages
